CHIEF COMPLAINT
Upper respiratory infection symptoms.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Randy Gutierrez is a 5-year-old male presenting with symptoms that began around supper time last night. Patient has developed a runny nose with nasal congestion and clear nasal mucous. He has a non-barky cough. Patient has been pulling on his ears and rubbing his nose frequently. Rectal temperature was measured at 100.3°F this morning. Appetite has been variable—he consumed about 7 ounces from a bottle this morning but then barely finished a second bottle and refused cereal. Patient is irritable and has difficulty sleeping despite having good energy. Exposure history includes sick older sister at home and recent playdate with nephew who had a sinus infection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Respiratory: Runny nose, nasal congestion with clear mucous, non-barky cough. ENT: Ear pulling bilaterally, nasal congestion. General: Low-grade fever, irritability, difficulty sleeping, decreased appetite. Skin: Worsening cradle cap noted.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cradle cap.

MEDICATIONS
Saline nasal mist, Tylenol given early this morning, baby Vicks applied to feet last night, humidifier use.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older sister currently ill with similar symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with parents and older sister. Recent exposure to sick contacts.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally. Ears: Otoscopic exam unremarkable. General appearance and examination otherwise within normal limits.

RESULTS
COVID-19: Negative.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Viral upper respiratory infection with nasal congestion and cough. Patient does not currently require antibiotics. Plan: Continue fluids and rest. Prescribe cough medicine (sister's medication) to have on hand—use half teaspoon dose for 5 days only if barking cough develops. Recommend Zarbee's cough syrup (pediatric under 1 year dose) for regular cough symptoms. Continue saline mist and humidifier use. Regarding cradle cap: Use antidandruff shampoo (Head & Shoulders, Selsun Blue, or Nizoral AD regular strength) twice weekly, continue soft brush with baby oil to remove scales, avoid eyes during rinsing. Expect improvement within 6 weeks. Follow-up appointment in one week. Patient to call if symptoms worsen, particularly if barking cough develops.
